newsitem.title: ITALY: BOI's Fazio says inflation not completely beaten.
newsitem.headline: BOI's Fazio says inflation not completely beaten.

text.p: The governor of the Bank of Italy Antonio Fazio said on Saturday the central bank would aim to keep inflation below two percent in 1998.
Speaking at the central bank's annual assembly, Fazio said: "We are aiming in 1998 for a variation of consumer prices contained within two percent, with substantial stability in producer prices."
Fazio said inflationary expectations had been beaten but that inflationary flames had not been completely doused.
"Inflationary expectations and inflation have been beaten," said Fazio. "The flames of inflation have not been completely extinguished," he added.
Preliminary data for May show consumer price inflation running at 1.5/1.6 percent year-on-year. Rome newsroom +396-6782505
